body: An exponent shows repeated multiplication when it is a positive whole number. In base ten, ten to the third power is 10 × 10 × 10, or one thousand. A negative integer exponent gives a reciprocal. Ten to the power of minus three is one thousandth.

Scientific notation can express a value as a number with magnitude at least one and less than ten multiplied by a power of ten. For example, 3,200 may be written as 3.2 × 10³. Multiplying a quantity by ten changes it by one order of magnitude. Comparing widely different scales becomes easier when both are expressed in the same units.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: Writing a value with a power of ten does not make a measurement more accurate. Units, significant figures and uncertainty describe different aspects of the measurement.
purpose: Show how powers express size changes across microscopic and astronomical scales.
